Inspired by Northern Nigeria's creativity, we build practical solutions to real-world challenges through tech, science, and collaboration. Interests: software, AI, data science, space, robotics, engineering.
summary:
Space is an incredible place to explore, but it also puts the human body through challenges that we cannot ignore. Injuries, muscle loss, reduced physical strength and other effects of living in microgravity can make recovery difficult, especially when astronauts are far away from Earth.

**ASTRA RECOVER** is our proposed software solution to help astronauts manage physical recovery and rehabilitation during space missions. It brings together recovery assessments, personalised clinician-approved rehabilitation plans, exercise session tracking and progress monitoring in one platform. It also gives medical teams on Earth a way to review recovery records and support astronauts in making informed decisions.

We designed ASTRA RECOVER with the realities of space missions in mind, including limited connectivity and the need for reliable offline access.

Our goal is simple: to help astronauts not only stay healthy in space, but also recover, rebuild their strength and remain better supported throughout their missions.
details:
Project Details — ASTRA RECOVER

ASTRA RECOVER is designed to support astronauts through injury rehabilitation and physical recovery during space missions. The idea is to make recovery easier to monitor, organise and manage, even when astronauts are far away from medical facilities on Earth.

The platform brings several important functions together. Astronauts can maintain their recovery profiles, complete physical assessments, view their approved rehabilitation plans, record exercise sessions and monitor changes in their recovery over time. Rather than simply recording whether an exercise was completed, the platform also helps track assessment results and other information that can give a clearer picture of recovery.

On the other side, medical professionals on Earth can review astronauts' recovery information, assess submitted records, monitor progress and provide appropriate medical guidance. This creates a connection between astronauts and their medical support teams, helping both sides stay informed.

One important factor we considered is communication in space. Internet connectivity cannot always be guaranteed, so ASTRA RECOVER is designed around offline access and data synchronisation. This allows important records to be saved locally and synchronised when a connection becomes available.

The project has several potential benefits. It can help astronauts keep their rehabilitation activities organised, make recovery information easier to follow, support medical teams in reviewing changes over time and provide better continuity of care during long-duration missions. It is also designed to support both injury recovery and physical deconditioning, recognising that astronauts may need help rebuilding physical capacity after spending extended periods in microgravity.

What makes ASTRA RECOVER creative is its focus on the recovery journey as a connected process rather than treating health monitoring and exercise tracking as separate activities. It combines assessment, rehabilitation planning, exercise records, progress monitoring and medical review in one mission-aware platform.

Throughout the design, we considered the physical challenges of spaceflight, limited communication, the importance of reliable health records, the need for medical supervision and the fact that every astronaut's recovery journey may be different. ASTRA RECOVER is intended to support medical professionals, not replace them. It does not independently diagnose conditions or prescribe treatment.

Our development focused on a software-based solution, without requiring custom wearable hardware for the initial prototype. We use React.js, Tailwind + Shadcn, FireBase, IndexedDB (offline) and Recharts

Ultimately, we want ASTRA RECOVER to contribute to a future where astronauts are not only monitored while exploring space, but are also properly supported when they need to recover.
